item.text: {"chapter_id":"5B","answers":[{"question_id":"5B.1","answer":"The agenda was broadly prosperity-oriented in stated design: Tshisekedi’s programme prioritized macroeconomic stability, education, health coverage, employment, agriculture, infrastructure, diversification, mining, and poverty reduction (BATCH-0013-E007); he instructed that the 2023 budget prioritize health, education, rural development, and integrating infrastructure (BATCH-0023-E013), and PDL-145T targeted schools, health centres, administrative buildings, roads, and local resilience (BATCH-0010-E004; BATCH-0023-E001). Some implementation and outcome evidence is favorable: the government reported ongoing PDL-145T construction and free-primary-education implementation (BATCH-0023-E001; BATCH-0020-E012), while the World Bank associated free primary education with increased enrollment, though the policy and comparison predated 2023 (BATCH-0014-E004). However, much of the economic agenda remained plans, speeches, or partner-supported programmes rather than independently verified execution (BATCH-0013-E002; BATCH-0006-E010; BATCH-0010-E010). Adverse evidence includes the auction of oil blocks overlapping rainforest and protected areas, with major projected climate risks (BATCH-0001-E011; BATCH-0014-E007), and a World Bank assessment that growth would not improve living conditions without ambitious reforms (BATCH-0016-E013). The 2023 record therefore shows prosperity-oriented intent and some implementation, but mixed sustainability and attribution, with insecurity, poverty, and food insecurity remaining severe (BATCH-0013-E001; BATCH-0020-E003).","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0013-E007","BATCH-0023-E013","BATCH-0010-E004","BATCH-0023-E001","BATCH-0020-E012","BATCH-0014-E004"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0013-E002","BATCH-0006-E010","BATCH-0010-E010","BATCH-0001-E011","BATCH-0014-E007","BATCH-0016-E013","BATCH-0013-E001","BATCH-0020-E003"],"limitations_and_gaps":["Independent evidence on the full executed budget, rent-seeking controls, and nationwide household outcomes is limited.","Several favorable results involve donor or partner support and cannot be attributed solely to Tshisekedi."]},{"question_id":"5B.2","answer":"The evidence establishes repeated presidential appointments and reshuffles, including the March 2023 cabinet changes and appointments in finance, economy, defense, interior, planning, health, and education (BATCH-0009-E003). Tshisekedi also appointed managers and board chairs across public enterprises and regulators, including statistics, entrepreneurship, agriculture, transport, employment, minerals, and state enterprises (BATCH-0008-E014), and met newly appointed Gécamines leaders to discuss management of national mining assets (BATCH-0018-E004). There is some evidence of formal professionalization: the World Bank reported competitive appointments for power and water utilities and the road fund (BATCH-0014-E002), and the central bank independently raised its policy rate while maintaining a pact against monetary financing (BATCH-0023-E020). Conversely, the index provides little evidence of selection criteria, qualifications, operational independence, performance reviews, or retention and replacement based on results (BATCH-0009-E003; BATCH-0008-E014; BATCH-0018-E005). Judicial appointments and removals were presidential and included dismissals, retirements, and compulsory resignations without stated reasons, raising independence concerns even though this is not direct economic-personnel evidence (BATCH-0015-E006; BATCH-0019-E006). The lens is therefore mixed and attribution is stronger for appointment authority than for professional quality or independence.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0009-E003","BATCH-0008-E014","BATCH-0018-E004","BATCH-0014-E002","BATCH-0023-E020"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0009-E003","BATCH-0008-E014","BATCH-0018-E005","BATCH-0015-E006","BATCH-0019-E006"],"limitations_and_gaps":["No systematic evidence links named appointees to economic performance or documents their freedom from political interference.","The strongest competitive-appointment evidence is World Bank-supported and institution-level rather than personally attributable."]},{"question_id":"5B.3","answer":"Formal fiscal and macroeconomic safeguards existed. The 2023 budget framework included revenue and expenditure documents, a medium-term budget framework, and a budget-risk statement (BATCH-0017-E005); the budget-governance decree required medium-term planning, fiscal-risk analysis, internal controls, audit committees, treasury planning, and publication of execution information (BATCH-0029-E003; BATCH-0029-E005). The government also adopted rules on public debt, mining royalties, carbon-credit proceeds, and land and real-estate transactions (BATCH-0015-E009; BATCH-0015-E010; BATCH-0024-E006; BATCH-0015-E008). Tshisekedi directed monetary, fiscal, and oversight authorities to stabilize the exchange rate and restrict non-priority spending (BATCH-0024-E005), while the independent central bank raised the policy rate and reported adherence to a no-monetary-financing pact (BATCH-0023-E020). Implementation and outcomes were weaker or mixed: 2023 revenues reached 91.22% of forecast, expenditures 96.49%, but inflation ended at 33.9% and annual-average inflation at 23.33% (BATCH-0022-E008); later parliamentary review cited incoherent spending, emergency procedures, uncertified debts, overruns, and noncompliance with public-finance rules (BATCH-0024-E003; BATCH-0024-E004). The ruler’s attribution is clearest for directives and formal policy, but not for central-bank decisions or each expenditure.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0017-E005","BATCH-0029-E003","BATCH-0029-E005","BATCH-0015-E009","BATCH-0015-E010","BATCH-0024-E006","BATCH-0015-E008","BATCH-0024-E005","BATCH-0023-E020"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0022-E008","BATCH-0024-E003","BATCH-0024-E004","BATCH-0010-E003"],"limitations_and_gaps":["The candidate index lacks a complete independent audit of monetary and fiscal implementation during 2023.","High inflation has multiple external and structural causes, so it cannot be assigned wholly to presidential choices."]},{"question_id":"5B.4","answer":"The administration adopted or supported formal rules relevant to economic activity, including the 2020 Telecom Law implementation, banking land and real-estate transaction rules, special economic-zone legislation, mining and export regulations, and procedures for state mining assets (BATCH-0014-E002; BATCH-0015-E008; BATCH-0015-E009; BATCH-0016-E011). The World Bank also reported stronger procurement procedures, digitized domestic revenue mobilization, and competitive appointments in utilities and the road fund (BATCH-0014-E002). Industrial-policy initiatives such as the battery-value-chain MOU and special-economic-zone planning indicate an effort toward diversification and value addition (BATCH-0013-E003; BATCH-0010-E011), but the MOU was nonbinding and lacked a concrete action plan or guaranteed financing (BATCH-0013-E004). Adverse evidence concerns enforcement and predictability: Reuters documented that a gas-auction bidder apparently lacked required financial records, initially ranked last, and was later moved to first after a changed technical score; ministerial intervention was alleged but denied and no final investigation is recorded (BATCH-0009-E007; BATCH-0009-E008). Mining communities also faced forced evictions, inadequate consultation and compensation, and weak grievance mechanisms (BATCH-0010-E018; BATCH-0004-E002). Thus formal rule-making was partly constructive, but consistent fair enforcement and protection of property and investment rights remain uncertain.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0014-E002","BATCH-0015-E008","BATCH-0015-E009","BATCH-0016-E011","BATCH-0013-E003","BATCH-0010-E011"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0013-E004","BATCH-0009-E007","BATCH-0009-E008","BATCH-0010-E018","BATCH-0004-E002"],"limitations_and_gaps":["The index contains limited evidence on entrepreneurship, labor-market enforcement, ordinary property disputes, and nationwide regulatory consistency.","The auction evidence documents irregularities and allegations but not a completed finding of personal presidential responsibility."]},{"question_id":"5B.5","answer":"There were some formal and institutional anti-capture measures: the government reported treasury, procurement, revenue, mining-asset, and extractive-transparency reforms (BATCH-0014-E002), strengthened CENAREF and related anti-corruption institutions (BATCH-0019-E003; BATCH-0019-E004), adopted mining-royalty and carbon-credit distribution rules (BATCH-0015-E010; BATCH-0024-E006), and initiated renegotiation of the Sicomines arrangement after an EITI study identified deviations from its infrastructure commitments and an undisclosed amendment (BATCH-0011-E007). EITI also recorded strong public debate and open-data publication, and the DRC received an improved implementation score, though beneficial-ownership disclosure remained incomplete (BATCH-0029-E007; BATCH-0029-E008). Countervailing evidence is substantial: the 2023 gas auction showed apparent eligibility and scoring irregularities, with denials but no final investigation (BATCH-0009-E007; BATCH-0009-E008); the State Department reported ineffective anti-corruption enforcement, phantom civil-servant payments, opaque special accounts, and official complicity in illicit mineral trade (BATCH-0011-E013); and parliamentary review identified overruns, uncertified debts, and works lacking visible field action (BATCH-0024-E003; BATCH-0024-E004). Mining-related evictions and inadequate remedies further indicate weak protection against connected or state-linked interests (BATCH-0010-E018). The record supports partial formal reform but weak and uneven enforcement, with no clear proof that Tshisekedi personally directed the alleged capture.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0014-E002","BATCH-0019-E003","BATCH-0019-E004","BATCH-0015-E010","BATCH-0024-E006","BATCH-0011-E007","BATCH-0029-E007","BATCH-0029-E008"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0009-E007","BATCH-0009-E008","BATCH-0011-E013","BATCH-0024-E003","BATCH-0024-E004","BATCH-0010-E018"],"limitations_and_gaps":["No independent finding identifies Tshisekedi as personally benefiting from or ordering the alleged favoritism.","Audit cooperation, procurement enforcement, sanctions, and recovery of losses are incompletely documented."]},{"question_id":"5B.6","answer":"The government allocated substantial stated attention and resources to productive public investment. Tshisekedi instructed that investment spending prioritize health, education, rural development, and national infrastructure (BATCH-0023-E013); PDL-145T planned schools, health centres, administrative buildings, feeder roads, and local development, with reported construction launched in 48 territories and hundreds of works described as ready by August (BATCH-0023-E001; BATCH-0019-E009). Free primary education and free maternity-care measures also supplied potentially broad public goods, while World Bank-supported education and governance projects added external financing and technical capacity (BATCH-0014-E003; BATCH-0014-E004). However, much evidence concerns appropriations, procurement, or government claims rather than verified quality and completion (BATCH-0006-E010; BATCH-0010-E010; BATCH-0023-E002). The WFP resilience programme fully implemented only half of planned activities, and monitoring coordination was weak (BATCH-0002-E001; BATCH-0002-E004). Parliamentary review found budget overruns, uncertified debts, and works with no observed field action (BATCH-0024-E004), while insecurity closed more than 2,000 schools and left health infrastructure fragile in conflict areas (BATCH-0022-E010; BATCH-0008-E002). The record therefore shows real implementation activity and some outputs, but uneven execution, major partner dependence, and uncertain nationwide quality and distribution.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0023-E013","BATCH-0023-E001","BATCH-0019-E009","BATCH-0014-E003","BATCH-0014-E004"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0006-E010","BATCH-0010-E010","BATCH-0023-E002","BATCH-0002-E001","BATCH-0002-E004","BATCH-0024-E004","BATCH-0022-E010","BATCH-0008-E002"],"limitations_and_gaps":["Independent completion, quality, procurement, and service-use data for PDL-145T are sparse.","Many education, health, and resilience outputs involve donors, UN agencies, or implementing partners."]},{"question_id":"5B.7","answer":"The administration created or used several evidence and monitoring mechanisms: the CPVS presidential monitoring roadmap tracked commitments and acknowledged implementation difficulties (BATCH-0020-E011; BATCH-0020-E012); education authorities held an annual performance review and monitored reform recommendations (BATCH-0023-E006); the government validated education-system diagnostics and supported World Bank evidence-based project design (BATCH-0009-E006; BATCH-0026-E009); and PDL-145T officials announced a telephone-based project-monitoring mechanism (BATCH-0023-E003). Fiscal rules also required reporting, internal audit, risk management, and publication of budget and execution information (BATCH-0029-E005). The ruler sometimes acknowledged problems, including declining purchasing power and difficulties in implementing health and maternity commitments (BATCH-0015-E004; BATCH-0020-E012), and directed macroeconomic corrective measures (BATCH-0024-E005). But independent evaluation and correction were inconsistent: the WFP evaluation found only half of planned activities fully implemented and weak monitoring coordination, with no evidence that recommendations were adopted (BATCH-0002-E001; BATCH-0002-E004; BATCH-0002-E005). CENI announced audits, yet outside observers later reported incomplete register transparency and rejected independent audit requests (BATCH-0017-E003; BATCH-0013-E009). Budget review also identified noncompliance and unobserved works (BATCH-0024-E003; BATCH-0024-E004). The evidence supports some monitoring and acknowledgment, but not reliable, independent, consequence-linked correction across the economic system.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0020-E011","BATCH-0020-E012","BATCH-0023-E006","BATCH-0009-E006","BATCH-0026-E009","BATCH-0023-E003","BATCH-0029-E005","BATCH-0015-E004","BATCH-0024-E005"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0002-E001","BATCH-0002-E004","BATCH-0002-E005","BATCH-0017-E003","BATCH-0013-E009","BATCH-0024-E003","BATCH-0024-E004"],"limitations_and_gaps":["Most monitoring evidence is official or programme-level and does not establish independent use of findings.","The index rarely documents a completed corrective action linked explicitly to an adverse economic evaluation."]},{"question_id":"5B.8","answer":"There are some distribution-oriented policies and allocations. PDL-145T was explicitly intended to reduce poverty and spatial inequalities through local schools, health centres, and administrative buildings (BATCH-0008-E010), and the carbon-credit order allocated proceeds among the Treasury, provinces, decentralized entities, and an environmental fund, with a planned implementation evaluation (BATCH-0024-E006). Free primary education, free maternity care, and social-protection programmes were directed toward poorer households and women, while the World Bank reported increased enrollment and gender-focused education investments (BATCH-0014-E004; BATCH-0026-E009). The government also acknowledged that purchasing-power gains had not sufficiently reached poorer people (BATCH-0015-E004). Adverse evidence shows persistent unequal incidence: poverty remained 62.3 percent in 2022, climate shocks disproportionately threatened poor, women, and excluded groups, and food insecurity affected more than 25 million people (BATCH-0001-E017; BATCH-0020-E009). Mining communities experienced forced evictions, destruction of homes and crops, inadequate compensation, and weak remedies (BATCH-0010-E018), while women and marginalized groups remained underrepresented and services were highly unequal across conflict-affected regions (BATCH-0028-E011; BATCH-0022-E010). The record therefore supports inclusion-oriented intent and some targeted mechanisms, but actual incidence across classes, regions, genders, and groups is mixed and often adverse.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0008-E010","BATCH-0024-E006","BATCH-0014-E004","BATCH-0026-E009","BATCH-0015-E004"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0001-E017","BATCH-0020-E009","BATCH-0010-E018","BATCH-0028-E011","BATCH-0022-E010"],"limitations_and_gaps":["The index lacks comprehensive incidence data for taxes, wages, benefits, regional investment, and household consumption in 2023.","Several distributional claims rely on planned rules or government reporting rather than independent evaluation."]},{"question_id":"5B.9","answer":"The principal documented shocks were conflict, displacement, food insecurity, currency depreciation, and inflation. Tshisekedi convened security and economic coordination meetings, pursued regional and international responses, directed macroeconomic stabilization measures, and announced targeted food-price and monetary interventions (BATCH-0021-E001; BATCH-0024-E005; BATCH-0007-E008). The government also continued PDL-145T, free education, health measures, and humanitarian cooperation during the crisis (BATCH-0010-E004; BATCH-0010-E006). There were some monitoring and corrective elements: the central bank raised its policy rate in response to risks (BATCH-0023-E020), and the president acknowledged that purchasing power was worsening and assigned follow-up to fiscal and monetary authorities (BATCH-0015-E004; BATCH-0015-E005). Outcomes remained severe: inflation reached 33.9 percent at year end, the franc depreciated by more than 28 percent, and displacement reached roughly 6.8–6.9 million (BATCH-0022-E008; BATCH-0010-E003; BATCH-0013-E014). Food insecurity exceeded 25 million, while humanitarian agencies faced major funding gaps (BATCH-0020-E009; BATCH-0020-E010). Conflict actors, regional intervention, global conditions, and donor financing materially constrain attribution. The evidence therefore shows timely announcements and some funded institutional responses, but limited proof of effective targeting, monitoring, or correction sufficient to offset the shocks.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0021-E001","BATCH-0024-E005","BATCH-0007-E008","BATCH-0010-E004","BATCH-0010-E006","BATCH-0023-E020","BATCH-0015-E004","BATCH-0015-E005"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0022-E008","BATCH-0010-E003","BATCH-0013-E014","BATCH-0020-E009","BATCH-0020-E010"],"limitations_and_gaps":["The index provides little independent evidence on the actual targeting, funding, and effects of announced price and monetary interventions.","The severe outcomes cannot be attributed solely to Tshisekedi because armed conflict, regional actors, global prices, and humanitarian funding shortfalls were major causal factors."]},{"question_id":"5B.10","answer":"The inherited-to-left trajectory is mixed rather than clearly stronger. There are credible signs of institution-building and social investment: the government pursued macroeconomic and procurement reforms, free primary education, PDL-145T, health-coverage measures, extractive-sector renegotiation, and formal fiscal-risk and audit rules (BATCH-0014-E002; BATCH-0014-E004; BATCH-0010-E004; BATCH-0011-E007; BATCH-0029-E003; BATCH-0029-E005). Some outcomes were favorable or improving, including increased public-primary enrollment, reported infrastructure construction, and a decline in documented human-rights violations from 2022 to 2023, though the latter is not an economic outcome and has reporting limitations (BATCH-0014-E004; BATCH-0019-E009; BATCH-0025-E009). Against this, 2023 ended with 33.9 percent inflation, more than 28 percent currency depreciation, over 25 million people in crisis or emergency food insecurity, and approximately 6.8–6.9 million internally displaced (BATCH-0022-E008; BATCH-0010-E003; BATCH-0020-E009; BATCH-0013-E014). The World Bank warned that growth would not translate into improved living conditions without ambitious reforms, while poverty, infrastructure weakness, and climate vulnerability remained substantial (BATCH-0016-E013; BATCH-0013-E001). Capture, budget-execution weaknesses, forced mining evictions, and uneven implementation further qualify durability and fairness (BATCH-0011-E013; BATCH-0024-E004; BATCH-0010-E018). Economic growth claims are official and attribution is confounded by external conditions, donor programmes, predecessor policies, and conflict; therefore the record supports partial capacity and policy progress but not a demonstrated durable, broad-based improvement by the end of 2023.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0014-E002","BATCH-0014-E004","BATCH-0010-E004","BATCH-0011-E007","BATCH-0029-E003","BATCH-0029-E005","BATCH-0019-E009"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0022-E008","BATCH-0010-E003","BATCH-0020-E009","BATCH-0013-E014","BATCH-0016-E013","BATCH-0013-E001","BATCH-0011-E013","BATCH-0024-E004","BATCH-0010-E018","BATCH-0025-E009"],"limitations_and_gaps":["The index lacks a consistent 2018-to-2023 household-income, employment, inequality, productivity, and investment series tied to ruler-attributed policy.","Many positive programmes had implementation lags or substantial external financing, so 2023 is too early to establish durable effects."]}],"cross_lens_observations":[]}
